verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.015665 did not improve on the current best 1.013711 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Reducing MLP capacity to buy more steps made the model under-capacity, so the experiment should not have shrunk the 4x MLP expansion.

insight.hint: The bad choice was treating extra value-embedding tables as free capacity when they actually cost steps and undertrained within the fixed time budget.

judge.summary: The agent read the current train.py and experiment history, then chose a capacity-increase idea: the model used ResFormer-style value embeddings only on alternating layers, so it made them available on all layers by changing has_ve() to return True. It committed this one-line edit and ran the experiment. The run completed without crashing, but val_bpb was 1.015665, worse than the current best 1.013711, so the harness discarded the attempt.
judge.feedback: The decisive problem was the experimental premise, not a syntax or shape bug: making value embeddings active on all layers added parameters without meaningfully increasing the number of effective training tokens. The harness statistics show the run completed fewer steps and processed fewer total tokens than the current-best comparison (2019 steps / 264.6M tokens vs. 2063 steps / 270.4M tokens), so the added embedding-table capacity was not free and likely became undertrained within the fixed 5-minute budget. The first wrong move was selecting this parameter-only capacity increase as the experiment; a better experiment should have preserved or increased steps/tokens rather than adding memory-bound lookups and optimizer parameters that reduce throughput.
